planting.note: Plant 8-10 inch disease-free stem cuttings horizontally or at a slant, 2-4 inches deep, once soil has warmed well past 65°F; TMS 30572 establishes readily and tolerates poor soils.

directions: TMS 30572 is a landmark cassava variety bred at IITA's Ibadan station under breeder S.K. Hahn and widely released across Nigeria, carrying resistance to cassava mosaic disease introgressed from the wild relative Manihot glaziovii along with useful tolerance of cassava bacterial blight. Plants branch at roughly waist height with distinctive red petioles, and the white-fleshed storage roots are typically harvested 9 to 12 months after planting, historically outyielding local landraces by a wide margin even without added fertilizer. It performed well in both on-station and on-farm trials and was readily accepted by farmers. It remains one of the most widely grown improved cassava varieties across farmers' fields in Nigeria decades after release.
sources: IITA (International Institute of Tropical Agriculture) — Cassava Breeding Unit, Ibadan
S.K. Hahn, A.K. Howland, E.R. Terry — Cassava Breeding at IITA

planting.note: Plant disease-free stem cuttings horizontally 2-4 inches deep in well-drained soil once soil has warmed past 65°F; give this erect-growing variety full sun and generous spacing.

directions: TME 419 is an IITA-bred cassava variety released in Nigeria in 2005 that has since become one of the country's most widely grown improved lines. It shows strong field resistance to cassava mosaic disease, grows with an erect, easy-to-manage architecture, and bulks up roots carrying roughly 39 to 40 percent dry matter and starch content above 38 percent. Yields commonly exceed 25 to 35 tons per hectare on sandy-loam soils, and its high dry matter makes it a standard check variety for garri and cassava flour quality trials. Roots are typically harvested 10 to 12 months after planting, though they can be left in the ground considerably longer where in-field storage is preferred.
sources: IITA (International Institute of Tropical Agriculture) — Cassava Breeding Unit, Ibadan
National Root Crops Research Institute (NRCRI), Nigeria

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed well past last frost; this semi-erect line tolerates drought and poor soils once established, making it well suited to a single later-summer sowing in marginal rainfall areas.

directions: IT90K-277-2, known locally in parts of Nigeria as Sasakawa, is an IITA-bred cowpea that combines resistance to brown blotch and anthracnose with tolerance of aphid feeding. Plants are semi-erect with white seed and reach medium maturity around 75 to 85 days, making the variety well suited to intercropping systems common across northern Nigeria. It has become one of the more widely adopted improved cowpea lines in Kano and other parts of northern Nigeria, as well as in neighboring Cameroon, prized for combining disease tolerance with dependable grain yield. Like other improved cowpeas it is susceptible to Striga, so it performs best on fields without a heavy Striga seed bank.
sources: IITA (International Institute of Tropical Agriculture) — Cowpea Breeding Program, Ibadan

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed well past last frost, since okra germinates poorly in cool soil; this early-flowering variety rewards prompt, regular picking.

directions: NHAe47-4 is an improved okra variety bred and released by Nigeria's National Horticultural Research Institute (NIHORT), selected for early flowering and thick, tender fresh pods on short-to-medium, profusely branching plants. Field trials found it substantially outyielding local okra grown alongside it in the same conditions. Its deeply lobed leaves and compact habit make it easy to manage in smallholder plots, and the pods carry a yellowish mucilage valued in traditional Nigerian okra soups. The variety also shows useful tolerance of root-knot nematode, an advantage on fields with a history of nematode pressure.

planting.note: Direct sow 1-2 inches deep in blocks for reliable wind pollination once soil has warmed well past last frost; this open-pollinated variety is bred for moisture-stressed, rain-fed conditions.

directions: Melkassa-2 is an open-pollinated maize variety derived from the ZM521 population and released by Ethiopia's EIAR through the Melkassa Agricultural Research Center, as part of a long-running program breeding maize for drought-prone lowland and intermediate agro-ecologies. It carries white grain, reaches intermediate maturity around 130 days, and is grown specifically in rain-fed areas where moisture stress is common during the growing season. Reported yields run roughly 4.0 to 5.0 tons per hectare under rain-fed conditions and 5.0 to 6.5 tons per hectare with irrigation. Because farmers can save and replant seed each year, as an open-pollinated variety it remains an accessible option for smallholders without reliable access to hybrid seed.
sources: Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR) — Melkassa Agricultural Research Center
CIMMYT — maize seed system research in Ethiopia

common_name: Nasir Haricot Bean (Melkassa Red Market-Class Variety)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost risk has passed and soil has warmed; Nasir performs best at mid-elevation sites with moderate, reliable rainfall through pod fill.

directions: Nasir is a red haricot bean variety released by the Melkassa Agricultural Research Center under Ethiopia's EIAR, bred for the food-type cooking bean market rather than export. It matures in roughly 90 to 120 days and is adapted to elevations between about 1200 and 1800 meters, with reported seed yields often exceeding 2.5 tons per hectare under good management. Its red seed coat has made it one of the more marketable bean types in several Ethiopian growing regions, and it remains a mainstay of basic seed production among private seed farms working with EIAR and Melkassa. Grow it like other bush-type common beans, direct-sown in warm soil with even moisture through flowering and pod fill.
sources: Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR) — Melkassa Agricultural Research Center
